A supplyIts stated inventory die and usesGuaranteed charges equal to the die's faces
A recipeKnowledge of a particular productCrafting capability, tools or ingredients by itself
A serviceAn agreed attempt or period of workAutomatic Strong outcomes or unrestricted daily treatment
Information or accessA useful fact, route, introduction or permissionAuthority over everyone who hears of it

Put treasure where it belongs

Decide who owns an object and why it is there. A tool chest in a workshop, a road toll in a guard's pouch, and a carefully wrapped recipe in a cook's kit all tell something about their owners. The party can find useful goods without every creature carrying a purse calibrated to its CV.

Creature loot entries offer starting material. Adjust an individual's possessions to the scene before play: a bandit who has collected no tolls should not carry the same takings as one leaving a successful robbery. Keep the equipment required for its printed actions consistent with its description. Do not remove essential gear solely because the party might recover it.

Give rewards for resolving the problem. A negotiation that opens a route may fulfill the same contract as a fight. If rescuing a captive is the objective, payment should not secretly depend on defeating the captors afterward.

> Example: the crossing commission. A patron promises 80 coins to the company > for a rescue and safe access. Four heroes can divide that into 20 each. The rescued > workers also offer a Rope Coil and Lever and Wedges, each worth 5. If accepted, > those are two carried items, not 10 extra coins in addition to the items. The > party earns the contract payment whether it negotiates with the robbers or fights.

Selling and trading

Intact, useful gear sells for half its listed price, rounded down, or trades at full listed value with a willing trader. Pay a shortfall in coins. Unused trade value is not cash change, and a trade cannot be converted into coins or a cash-equivalent voucher at full value.

> Example: a recovered weapon. An ordinary melee weapon is worth 12 coins. > Selling it brings 6. A willing trader can instead accept it for 12 coins of goods: > a 5-coin rope, a 4-coin sleeping roll and a 3-coin water flask. The party cannot > trade it for a 12-coin credit note and immediately cash that note for 12 coins.

A market needs willing buyers as well as prices. Do not promise that a village will purchase unlimited identical goods. Equally, avoid inventing shortages only after a player has committed to a reasonable purchase. Establish unusual local conditions in advance and quote the offered price clearly.

Supplies with uncertain remaining quantities have no standard resale offer. A freshly acquired or crafted full supply can attract a half-price offer where there is demand. Special equipment needs an available buyer and an agreed valuation; apply the same half-sale/full-trade rule to that valuation. Gems and other treasure with a stated trade value do not suffer a second automatic halving.

Selling a card-granted item does not renew the grant. Learning an ability that uses a compatible item already owned does not create another copy to sell. The same ordinary weapon can serve several compatible attacks, with its Bulk counted once.

Supply is uncertain, not imaginary

After using an inventory supply, roll its die. On 1, step down: d20 → d12 → d10 → d8 → d6 → d4 → out. The use that empties it still works. The die tracks remaining supply without counting every arrow or mouthful.

A d4 healing bottle has a 25% chance to empty after each use. That does not mean it contains exactly four doses. A supply that has survived several checks remains at its current die until a check changes it.

The current market's healing bottles use d4: Lesser restores 6 HP, Greater 10, and Superior 16, before Life resistance and missing-HP limits. Their price buys potency as well as uncertain longevity. They do not require a healing spell roll or caster HP payment.

A potion still needs a free hand and the giver's Maneuver. A different recipient spends a Reaction unless at 0 HP. A bow, two-handed weapon, or weapon-and-shield combination occupies the hands that would otherwise use the bottle. Dropping an item is free; properly stowing it takes a Maneuver and can provoke. Apply those costs consistently to heroes and opponents.

Make special equipment personal

Ordinary weapons describe what the hero carries; their attack cards supply the mechanics. Special equipment adds the benefit actually printed on its card. A named sword does not acquire extra range or damage from its appearance alone.

An @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.7583def7f886433c]{Ember Edge} requires Flame 1 and adds 1 Fire damage to attacks made with that melee weapon, with Burning 1 on Strong. It does not turn a ranged attack into a compatible use. A hero may own it before meeting the requirement, but cannot use its special benefit until qualified.

A @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.48b5c622acdaf95f]{Cincture of Might} gives its printed Brawn benefit while worn. It does not stack with another positive Brawn item and does not recalculate creation DP or class eligibility. Use explicit card text for cursed items that suppress bonuses or set an attribute; a curse is not permission to invent a hidden exception after its bearer acts.

You can change an item's history and appearance to fit a campaign. A brass lens may come from a lighthouse or a buried observatory without changing its ability. Make mechanical changes explicit and review their effect on the party before introducing them as routine treasure.

Understanding what was found

An item states whether understanding is required to use it. Some magical weapons work at once; another object may require identification. Use the appropriate identification card and reveal what its outcome says. Possessing a mysterious object does not grant every fact about it, but ordinary inspection still reveals its visible form and obvious operation.

Give useful clues to dangerous properties. A written warning, an earlier owner's account or an observed effect lets the party investigate before committing. A curse can create a difficult decision without depending on the players having no chance to recognize risk.

Recipes, ingredients and work

Crafting requires an appropriate capability, a known recipe, its tools and actual ingredients. Cards that grant recipes provide those stated choices; additional recipes can come through Ordinary Recipe Study, discovery or derivation. They are not automatically available for coin purchase.

An identified object is not automatically a known recipe. Derivation uses its own ability, work intervals and cumulative target. Rare objects may require a long research project. Do not shorten that project through group rolls; neither crafting nor derivation uses group checks.

> Example: Bottled Morning. A crafter with this ability knows the Lesser Healing > Bottle recipe. With a mixing kit, moonmint, clean water and prepared life salts, > they spend one hour and roll Knowledge. The outcome raises one compatible supply > by 1/2/3 inventory steps, but the recipe's cap is d4. From out, any result therefore > produces a d4 bottle. Strong does not create three bottles or exceed the cap. > Check carried ingredients after the attempt. The recipe is not free stock.

The ordinary d6 material bundle costs 12 coins, while prepared healing ingredients cost 80 for their d6 bundle. Each bundle must contain the materials the recipe actually needs. Renaming common grass as life salts does not satisfy it. Foraging cards give practical ways to acquire suitable materials and deserve places where those materials can be found.

Services and lasting favors

A treatment appointment costs 10 coins for one eligible attempt; it does not promise complete recovery. Identification service likewise buys an attempt with the right capability, not a guaranteed Strong result. Daily limits still apply across different providers.

An ally might waive a fee, offer a workshop, or introduce a specialist as a reward. State the scope: one appointment, use of the bench for a week, or an introduction. This makes favors useful without turning every grateful person into a permanent source of unlimited labor. Hired people retain their own concerns and choices.

Campaigns and Lasting Consequences

Heroes of Legend · Dungeon Architect’s Guide & Bestiary

The company returns with the missing workers and a story the village will repeat for years. One hero returns with a scar. Another has spent the last Grit they were saving for a desperate hour. The road is open again, but the people who opened it have changed.

A campaign follows both kinds of consequence: what the heroes change in the world and what their adventures leave with them. Let victories last, let costs matter, and make room for the players to choose what comes next.

Award levels for meaningful progress

Use milestones when the heroes resolve an important problem, achieve a shared goal or reach a significant turning point. A negotiated settlement can qualify just as well as a battle. Tell the group what kind of progress you intend to recognize so they do not feel required to seek unnecessary fights.

At level 2 and every later level, award 8 + the new level DP. These points can be saved and spent in a place you judge safe. The character-creation DP adjustments from Knowledge, Reason and Guile apply only at levels 0 and 1, not to later awards.

Grit grants add the new point; they do not refund previous expenditure. Attributes and HP do not rise automatically with level. Cards may provide their explicit, limited increases. Discipline ranks are purchased in sequence at class prices, and the hero must meet a card's requirements before buying it. There are no prerequisite-card chains or access to a second class's signatures.

> Example: reaching level 3. A hero receives 11 DP, gains one Grit and chooses > a level-3 signature from their class. They can now buy eligible Adept cards, but > still need those cards' discipline requirements. Their base attributes and HP > remain the same unless a specific purchase or effect changes them.

Review the group's new choices before preparing the next adventure. A new route, healing option or area attack can change what an obstacle asks of the party. Do not immediately make every new ability ineffective; give the players a chance to enjoy the choice they made.

Safe places and downtime

A safe place is a judgment about the situation, not a magical property of an inn. A guarded camp may be safe; a room above a hostile tavern may not. Explain the reason when the party asks whether it can spend DP or take a breath. Do not move the standard simply because you hoped to keep them under pressure.

Distinguish a safe breath from longer work. HP recovery does not complete a four-hour fitting attempt, buy ingredients or advance a research project by a day. For downtime, ask each player what they do, record the required time and resources, and resolve only consequential uncertainty.

Track the wound receiving treatment, its accumulated recovery progress and whether it has had today's attempt. Track crafting by recipe and supply; track derivation by its own interval and target. Several heroes can pursue different projects, but they cannot pool group rolls into crafting, derivation or treatment.

Grit is a lasting resource

Characters begin with 2 Grit at level 1 and gain a point at levels 3 and 7. A once-only learned card can provide another. Ordinary rest does not refill it. Keep both grants and expenditure visible, so the player knows what remains when a dangerous choice arrives.

Do not use a fixed quota of encounters to grind away Grit. Give dangers understandable stakes and opportunities to prepare, negotiate or withdraw. Choosing to risk a remaining point for a companion should feel like the player's decision. A campaign can remain challenging through objectives, rivals and changed circumstances without making every journey an unavoidable sequence of fights.

When a hero reaches 0 HP

A player character enters Dying, immediately suffers a new wound, and follows the survival procedure. Ordinary creatures and NPCs die at 0 instead; they do not automatically gain the heroes' death rolls or Grit. A summoned form disappears.

Roll 3d6 plus one die per prior wound, capped at five dice total. Keep the highest three, sort them from low to high, and read them as a three-digit result. The new wound joins the count after this roll. Treatment never removes a scar from the count.

Choose the table for the largest damage component after resistance; the player chooses ties. When all components were resisted and only the minimum 1 damage causes the wound, the player chooses among the attack's original damage types. Physical includes force and sonic. Fire, Cold and Lightning share Elemental wounds but retain separate resistances. Mental, Radiant and Life/Necrotic each have a table.

> Example: the second wound. A hero with one prior wound rolls 2, 4, 4 and 6. > Keep 4, 4, 6 and read 446, not fourteen. If the attack dealt 2 Physical and > 1 Fire but both were fully resisted, the minimum damage still applies and the > player chooses Physical or Elemental for that result.

If a body part is absent or the result cannot apply, advance to the next listed result, such as 116 to 122, until an applicable entry is reached. Do not reroll for a more convenient wound. All tables end at 666.

Keep the survival choice clear

At the start of a Dying turn, the player chooses to spend one Grit or make a death roll. That choice stands for the turn; they cannot see the roll before deciding. Spending Grit restores full HP but preserves the wound.

Fortitude death rollResult
WeakAdd 1 death mark.
StandardNo change.
StrongStabilize at 0 HP and clear death marks.
Retained natural 111Add 2 death marks instead of the ordinary Weak result.
Retained natural 666Restore 1 HP and clear death marks.

At three death marks, the character enters Last Words. Damage while already Dying adds one mark per damaging event, not another wound. Damage that returns a stabilized character to Dying causes a new wound and adds one mark.

The universal Stabilize Maneuver targets an adjacent Dying PC, clears their marks and leaves them at 0 HP, unable to act. Healing above 0 clears marks and ends HP-caused unconsciousness, but does not remove an unrelated condition. A safe breath cannot be used to skip an unresolved Dying procedure.

Run this moment carefully. State the current HP, marks, Grit and relevant conditions. Other players can decide how to help, but the fallen hero's player chooses whether to spend their Grit.

Treatment removes effects, not history

Each wound identifies its lasting penalties, required treatment and Recovery Value, or RV. Use the appropriate card and its full work interval. Weak, Standard and Strong add 1/2/3 recovery progress. Each wound can receive only one treatment attempt per day across all healers.

When progress reaches RV, remove exactly the listed treatable effects. The scar and wound count remain. A separate temporary condition uses its normal decay or removal; it does not restart because the wound is still recorded.

> Example: a shoulder wound. Physical 333 applies Bleeding 1 and a lasting > Bane to physical activities. Bleeding resolves and decays, or can be reduced > appropriately. Soft Tissue treatment needs RV 3 to remove the Bane. Standard > treatment adds 2 on one day; Weak adds 1 on the next, completing treatment. > The scar remains and counts toward later wound rolls.

Use the broad language of physical or mental activities when applying wound Banes. Decide whether the injury matters to the task rather than requiring an argument about exactly which joint moved. Cosmetic and social consequences should likewise follow the entry; treatment that removes both a social Boon and Bane removes both.

A replacement limb is a real project. The Simple Replacement Leg recipe makes a prosthesis; Fit a Replacement then fits it and relieves only the penalties the wound allows it to relieve. Owning a wooden leg does not itself erase a movement penalty, regrow a limb or remove the scar. A rest remedy applies only when printed.

Last Words and what follows

A wound result of 666, or three death marks, begins Last Words. The character can speak and do nothing else. They die at the end of the second following turn. Ordinary healing, treatment, potions and Grit cannot reverse this. Only an explicit exceptional ability could say otherwise.

Give that time to the player. They may offer a warning, name a successor, speak to a friend or remain silent. Do not require a speech or turn the moment into a test of performance. Resolve any abilities triggered by hearing Last Words according to their own text.

Afterward, let the group decide what the company does. A funeral, a journey home or a promise to finish the work may matter more than immediately introducing another threat. Discuss a replacement character promptly so the player can return to active participation. Agree on entry circumstances and starting resources openly; this book does not impose an unreviewed universal replacement package.

Capture, retreat and retirement

Attacks are lethal unless an explicit ability provides a different outcome. Ordinary opponents die at 0 HP. To take a prisoner, secure surrender while they can still choose it or use grappling and restraint. Do not let an attacker declare all their lethal damage nonlethal after the outcome.

When escape is possible, describe it. Withdrawing may cost equipment, position or an objective, but those consequences should follow the scene. Do not promise safety and then invent pursuit that the opposition had no way to organize.

A player may choose retirement before death. Their hero can become a local ally, a mentor or someone the next company hopes to impress. Preserve that person's achievements without turning them into a free source of unlimited abilities or supplies. The campaign's continuity comes from its relationships and consequences, not from requiring the same four people to survive every chapter.

Using the Bestiary

Heroes of Legend · Dungeon Architect’s Guide & Bestiary

Dry clicking answers the heroes' footsteps. Scraps tied to a ruined wall mark a safe path through the debris. Coins beneath a bridge have been sorted with surprising care. Before a creature attacks, it can already tell the players something about the place they have entered.

The bestiary gives you creatures to portray and complete cards to run. Use the signs, purpose and counterplay alongside the statistics. A creature is more useful when you know why it is here and what might make it leave.

Read from the top down

Every creature's name includes its current CV. Beneath a short description, find its six attributes, HP, Speed, Size, Armor DR, Evasion, Threat and Stability on the left, with weaknesses, resistances and immunities on the right. Unique actions come next, with defense, damage type and complete outcomes in the table. Details below describe the action, its targets and any remaining limits. The final section collects healing, senses, signs, motives and encounter guidance.

FieldUse during play

HPIts immediate endurance. Ordinary creatures die at 0 unless an explicit exception applies.
SpeedIts available movement, subject to terrain and its printed movement modes.

ThreatBoons or Banes applied to player defenses against its attacks, unless an attack states an exception.

0 under Evasion or Threat means no modifier from that field. “1 Bane” means one Bane through the ordinary dice procedure, not minus one to a total.

Choose the moment to react

A creature’s distinctive Reaction competes with its opportunity attack for the same single Reaction. A duelist may save it to turn a blade, a guardian to cover a companion, or a dragon to sweep a damaging attacker away. Read the trigger before the dice: interference comes before the roll, protection before the damage, and retaliation after the incoming attack resolves. A creature that dies or loses the required capability cannot retaliate.

Several named movement Maneuvers trade distance for avoiding one chosen enemy’s opportunity attack. Other enemies still threaten the route. Converting the Maneuver into a full movement allowance remains useful when distance alone matters. Abilities belong only to the creatures that print them; a family name grants none. A summoned profile has its own permitted Maneuvers and no independent Reactions.

A Goblin Scrapper at the table

The @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.d65ecdabb2fc906b]{Goblin Scrapper} has CV 8, HP 8, Speed 7, Size 1, Armor DR 0, Evasion 1 Bane, Threat 0 and Stability 0. Its Scrap knife requires Agility defense and deals 5/3/2 physical damage for Weak/Standard/Strong player defense.

A hero attacking it suffers 1 Bane from Evasion. If the goblin has used Defend, that adds another Bane until its stated expiry. An applicable Boon cancels one; apply the usual net cap. The goblin does not roll to dodge the attack.

When the goblin uses Scrap knife, its target rolls Agility. On Standard defense, the attack deals 3 physical damage before resistance. A hero with Physical resistance 2 takes 1. On Strong defense, the attack deals 2 before resistance and still deals the minimum 1 total damage. The goblin's Agility +2 does not get added to that player's defense roll or to the knife's damage.

Slip the Rush lets the goblin spend its Reaction after a visible enemy ends voluntary movement adjacent to it, moving 1 square without an opportunity from that enemy. Other enemies still threaten the route. Spending it means the goblin has no Reaction left for an opportunity attack until its normal refresh.

On its turn, the goblin can use its Main Action for an attack and its Maneuver for Roll Away, moving up to two squares in a straight line without provoking. Roll Away still obeys terrain and occupied-square restrictions. Choosing it means the goblin did not spend that same Maneuver on Defend. Its purpose is to protect a salvage claim; a useful tool or a recognized claim may matter more to it than a fight.

Read complete outcomes

The DA card's damage columns read Weak defense / Standard defense / Strong defense. Weak is dangerous for the defending hero. Each slash separates a complete outcome, including conditions and movement. Do not combine the riders from several columns or apply a Strong-defense rider to every result.

A line such as “6 + Bleeding 2 / 4 + Bleeding 1 / 3” means exactly those three alternatives. The damage type has its own table column; range and target appear in the action's details. A zero-damage condition result remains a condition result; the minimum-damage rule does not invent damage for an effect that deals none.

Healing and other nonattack actions use their own details rather than this damage legend. A healing action's Strong result is beneficial when healing an eligible ally. When the same ability harms a healing-harmed target, use its printed harmful procedure and defense outcomes.

Actions are choices

A creature has the normal Main Action, Maneuver, Reaction and movement. Several attacks give options. A claw, bite and breath weapon do not all occur on one Main Action unless a printed action explicitly combines them.

Read a maneuver before deciding it fits. Check range, path, endpoint, duration and usage limits. Use the printed Reaction trigger and cost. Opportunity attacks use Basic Melee and occur before the provoking action; the original action continues if its actor is still capable. The specialty attack is not an opportunity substitute.

Mark expiring effects where you can see them. Defend adds a temporary Bane to player attacks against that creature; it does not change permanent Evasion. A shield's hunker consumes a Reaction; defense rolls do not.

Universal actions

Creature cards list their unique actions. The following universal choices are available when the creature is capable of performing them; they are not repeated on each card.

Damage defenses in order

For each damage component, add its applicable numerical weakness, then subtract its matching resistance. Use the highest value of a given type rather than adding several sources; the normal cap is 3. Do not add a weakness for a damage type the event never included. Apply minimum 1 damage to the whole damaging event after its components have been reduced.

> Example: mixed damage. An event deals 4 Physical and 1 Fire. Fire Weakness 2 > changes the Fire component to 3. Physical resistance 2 and Fire resistance 1 > leave 2 Physical plus 2 Fire, for 4 total. Armor DR and Physical resistance are > the same value, not two reductions.

A special vulnerability follows its own wording. Fire stops the Bridge Troll's Knit Flesh for the stated interval; it does not automatically add Fire damage. The troll recovers HP only while above 0 and cannot regenerate from death.

Forced movement and Stability

All actors start at Stability 0 unless an explicit trait, ability or item says otherwise. On creature cards, Heavy Frame identifies a permanent grant. A large footprint by itself grants none. Use the highest applicable source, maximum 3.

Deduct the initial target's Stability once before forced movement. Terrain then consumes movement by square: normal 1, difficult 2. Any positive remaining budget can enter the last square and stop even if its cost exceeds that budget.

When the moving creature or group strikes another movable creature, resolve collision damage from the movement remaining at contact. Apply applicable damage resistance, then deduct the new member's Stability. Continue as one group if movement remains. Never charge the same member's Stability twice during that movement.

> Example: a collision chain. Push 5 meets Stability 1, leaving 4. The target > crosses one normal square, leaving 3, then collides with a Stability-2 creature. > Both receive 3 collision damage before applicable resistance. Deduct the new > member's Stability 2, leaving 1 for further group movement.

A hard obstruction stops the group and adds 1 to the remaining-budget collision damage. Every member takes the applicable damage. Finish in separate legal spaces; if everyone cannot fit, stop at the last position where they can. You choose the arrangement without granting extra forward movement or passage through walls. The original mover bounces one square opposite afterward where possible.

Stability does not resist Prone, grapples, conditions or damage. If Stability prevents a push, the attack's other effects still occur.

Play purpose, not omniscience

A creature acts on what it can perceive and know. Use its senses as printed; ordinary hearing does not become precise location through any wall. Give players visible signs when a capability should be recognizable: a troll's closing wounds, a wolf's circling pack, or a sentinel that stops at a boundary.

The tactics line suggests useful choices. Adapt them to the scene without changing the card. A hungry animal might protect food, while one defending young risks more. A guard can retreat, surrender or negotiate while still alive. At 0 HP, an ordinary creature does not automatically receive a chance for last-minute stabilization.

Knowledge of a familiar fantasy trope can suggest an experiment, but only this creature's printed rules determine its effect. If a player tries something that would plainly fail here, offer information their hero could reasonably perceive before they spend an action on a mistaken assumption.

Summoned forms

Summons are energy shaped to resemble and act like creatures. They cannot receive healing and disappear at 0 HP without a body or permanent loot. They are still tangible: they occupy squares, block movement and can be damaged, pushed or grappled unless their own card states an exception.

A ring-and-spark marker in the upper-right corner identifies a summonable creature. Its label gives the category and minimum level: Animal 1, for example. Select the marker in the PDF to open that creature’s player profile. No marker means the creature is not an eligible summon.

Use the separate player profile for an eligible summon. Its attack outcomes run Weak to Strong attack, and its modifiers already express the player's perspective. Do not reverse the DA card mentally or import its independent Reactions. A creature is eligible only where the profile explicitly lists the relevant category and tier.

Controller spendsOne summon receives
Main ActionMain Action and Maneuver
ManeuverManeuver and movement

A summon receives at most one command on its controller's turn. The controller may spend Main and Maneuver on different summons. Normal downward conversion applies; a Main-command package does not also include free movement. Convert its Maneuver to movement if it must approach before attacking.

No command means no activity: no following, watching, alerting, helping or continued attack. Existing conditions and durations still resolve on the controller's turn. Commands cannot be saved for an enemy turn. Summons have no independent Reactions, opportunity attacks or summon chains.

Keep the nearest occupied squares of controller and summon within six squares, using ordinary grid distance. Exactly six is valid; beyond six it immediately disappears. Movement of either participant, including forced movement, can break the tether. It also disappears if the controller becomes unconscious or dies.

> Example: the Moon Hart. A commanded summoned hart uses Battle Mending. Its > controller pays 3 HP before resolution, bypassing resistance and remaining above > 0. The hart does not also pay. Roll the hart's Reason and heal 5/10/15, reduced > by the eligible recipient's Life resistance, minimum 1 where HP is missing. The > hart itself cannot be healed. Pay normal terrain costs and provoke normally. The ally must be conscious and not Paralyzed; an uncommanded summon cannot trigger this. No attack or command is granted, and movement granted by a free attack cannot trigger it.

Opportunity Attack: Basic Melee against the provoking creature. Spends its Reaction before the provoking action resolves. That action continues if the creature remains capable.

Pack Hunter: When attacking a target adjacent to another active ally, impose 1 additional Bane on that target’s defense (or gain 1 attack Boon when controlled). Unconscious, Paralyzed and uncommanded summoned allies do not qualify.

Healing: Living: ordinary HP healing applies.

Senses: Keen scent within 6 squares.

Signs: Parallel tracks keep to the downwind side of the trail.

Purpose: Drive intruders from a den or bring food back to it.

Target: One adjacent creature. Player defense: Agility. Damage type: physical.

Make Room

A clipped order sends one companion into the opening before it closes.

One willing active ally within 3 squares that can hear it may spend that ally’s Reaction to move up to 2 squares. Movement provokes normally and pays terrain costs. An uncommanded summon cannot act; summons have no Reaction to spend.

Rally at the Blow

A sharp call catches the wounded companion's attention before pain can turn into panic.

After a visible willing ally within 3 squares takes HP damage from an attack, reduce that ally's Frightened by 1 if it can hear this creature. Then give it 1 Boon on its next defense before the start of this creature's next turn; for an NPC ally impose 1 Bane on the corresponding player attack. A familiar rhythm cuts through panic and brings one companion back to the moment.

One willing ally within 3 squares that can hear it reduces either Frightened or Dazed by 1. Once per turn. This does not recalculate action categories already selected at turn start.

A sharp call catches the wounded companion's attention before pain can turn into panic.

After a visible willing ally within 3 squares takes HP damage from an attack, reduce that ally's Frightened by 1 if it can hear this creature. Then give it 1 Boon on its next defense before the start of this creature's next turn; for an NPC ally impose 1 Bane on the corresponding player attack. The defense benefit is consumed on that roll even if canceled and does not stack with itself. No healing or action is granted.

General details

Healing: Living: ordinary HP healing applies.

Senses: Ordinary sight and hearing.

Tactics and retreat: Keep the rhythm near frightened companions and use the staff to slow the party's momentum. Move with the wounded rather than abandon them.

Habitat: Settlement; frontier; contested road · Communication: Common and its community’s language

Loot: Ordinary carried gear and 8 coins; special rewards belong to the adventure.

Creating and Adapting Creatures

Heroes of Legend · Dungeon Architect’s Guide & Bestiary

Begin with the creature's place in the adventure. What will the heroes notice? What does it want? What does it do when threatened? A distinctive answer to these questions often matters more than another attack.

Use an existing creature whose play pattern is close to what you need. Changing its appearance, name or allegiance may be enough. If you change its mechanics, record the new values explicitly and review its CV as an estimate. A renamed creature should not acquire hidden abilities during the fight.

Build the table experience first

Write a short description of the creature itself, then choose one recognizable combat behavior. A predator separates prey; a sentinel holds a route; a spirit makes approaching it unsettling. Select printed actions that express that behavior. Give the heroes signs and counterplay they can discover.

Add another action only when it creates a useful choice. A bite that does exactly what the claw does adds reading without changing a decision. A bite that holds a target, at the cost and restrictions of grappling, can change the fight. Do not grant every creature a complex suite merely because the book has room.

Use the normal action economy. Mark each ability Main, Maneuver, Reaction or Passive; print its trigger, target, range, shape, outcomes, duration and limits as applicable. A powerful breath can be a Main Action with a printed use restriction. “Procedure: Breath” is not an action cost.

Fill the card completely

PartCheck before using it
IdentityName, CV, description of appearance and nature
AttributesAll six, including attack attributes needed for player control
Body and defensesHP, Speed/modes, footprint, physical DR, Evasion, Threat, Stability
Damage interactionsWeakness, resistance, immunities and healing behavior
ActionsFull defense outcomes, ranges, target attributes, costs and limits
Other capabilitiesPassives, senses, communication and explicit exceptions
Adventure useSigns, purpose, tactics, retreat, counterplay, habitat and loot
SummoningExplicit eligibility and separate profile, or ineligible

Armor DR is physical resistance. The list repeats that number for clarity; it does not add another reduction. Use Boons and Banes for Evasion and Threat, not a new target number or an unexplained signed statistic. Nonzero Stability needs an explicit grant and remains capped at 3.

Write DA attacks in defense order. If an attack produces 2/4/6 on Weak/Standard/Strong attacker outcomes, its ordinary defense table reads 6/4/2. Reverse the whole outcome, including conditions and displacement, not just the damage. Store the player-facing version for any eligible summon and check both against each other.

Use monster abilities as construction tools

The separate monster catalog contains abilities with no DP price or player discipline requirements. A creature has an ability only if its own entry grants it. Players cannot buy one simply because they meet a similarly named discipline.

Copy the applicable effect into the creature's authored entry and specialize its printed values where the template calls for that. Preserve targeting, costs, limits and counterplay. A template is not permission to leave “see ability” in a combat action that needs a second lookup to resolve.

An animal form or summoned category does not inherit this entire library. A summoned profile must restrict activity to paid commands, remove independent Reactions and state its own allowed actions. Being a spirit does not automatically grant movement through walls; being a construct does not automatically grant every condition immunity.

Estimate CV transparently

The current estimate uses CV = ceiling(3 × sqrt(E × O) × U), minimum 1. It is a comparison tool with explicit assumptions, not a complete model of combat.

InputCurrent seed definition
IExpected damage of a reference hero's attack against the creature, after Evasion and physical resistance
E(Creature HP + two turns of its printed regeneration) ÷ I
OExpected damage of its reference attack against the reference defender, multiplied by expected targets
UA recorded judgment for capabilities not directly represented above

The reference hero has attribute +1 and physical attack outcomes 3/5/7. Enumerate the actual 3d6 outcomes, with extra dice for Evasion and the correct retained-three procedure. Apply resistance and minimum damage per event. The reference defender also uses +1, with Physical resistance 1 and other resistances 0. Threat changes the defense distribution. Use the creature's printed target expectation and reference attack for O; do not add its attack attribute to a player's defense probability.

The two regeneration turns are an assumption, not a prediction of fight length. The current U rubric starts at 1 for simple damage, with 1.50–1.65 for substantial combined utility, healing or repeated disabling pressure. A major package with useful Maneuvers and Reactions may reach 1.70–1.85. Those values are judgments, not proven prices for conditions. Keep your assumptions with your own creature notes so you can revisit them after play.

If a creature deals no direct damage, this formula cannot establish its contribution by multiplying by zero. Evaluate it in the mixed encounter it supports. Area damage, healing, repeated control and unreachable firing positions also need explicit tests. Do not disguise their uncertainty behind a precise-looking CV.

Test the choice the creature creates

First run the creature with ordinary companions and modest terrain against actual characters. Record their cards, defenses, supplies and tactics. Test a stronger terrain advantage separately. If the creature has a counter, record whether players could discover it and whether using it was worthwhile.

Look beyond total damage. A creature can be numerically survivable and unpleasant because it removes too many turns. Another can die quickly but create a memorable rescue or movement puzzle. Revise the action or situation responsible instead of raising all numbers until the fight lasts longer.

For a new summon, also test command affordability, the initial free command, tether pressure and the cost of replacing a lost form. Check that uncommanded forms provide no active scouting, alerts or attacks. A summoned healer charges its controller; the form cannot receive healing. These restrictions are part of its actual play value.

After a change, recalculate the estimate and check the creature's full outcome text. A content audit can catch missing fields or arithmetic errors. Only play can tell you whether the creature delivers the intended experience.

Heroes of Legend · Dungeon Architect’s Guide & Bestiary

These 126 monster-only abilities are tools for preparing and adapting creatures. They are separate from learned player abilities, with no DP price or permission to purchase them. A creature gains only the abilities printed in its own entry.

Templates may describe attacker outcomes for construction. During play, use the creature's complete defense-outcome table or the appropriate summoned player profile. Per-creature values and restrictions govern where they specialize a template.

Entries follow in alphabetical order. Their mechanical text comes directly from the authored monster catalog. The assembled reference omits editorial status lines and shared navigation links; it retains every specific action, effect and limit.

Every step drags an invisible chain back toward the thing it cannot abandon.

Rules

ID: monster-anchor-bound

Action: Passive

The entry names a visible anchor and its interaction. Destroying or resolving that anchor has only the printed effect. Unless stated otherwise, the creature dies at 0 and does not regenerate a new body. A story hook is not automatic immunity.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Rules

ID: monster-battle-mending

Action: Main Action; spell

One visible adjacent living creature; free hand required. Pay the printed life cost first, bypassing resistance, and remain above 0 HP. A player controller rolls the creature’s printed healing attribute for its printed HP outcomes. For a hostile NPC healing an ally, ask a player to make that same creature-attribute roll, including its applicable Boons/Banes. The DA still chooses its action and target; being the dice roller grants no control of the NPC. Life resistance reduces healing normally. This may instead target a healing-harmed creature: the result becomes Life damage, with Fortitude defense if a player is defending for that creature and no extra opposed roll. Keep the same range, life cost and free-hand requirement. This can be repeated while affordable. Provokes as spellcasting; no separate spell slots.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Action: Maneuver

Use the printed attack. Standard also applies the printed Burning 1 or Freezing 1; Strong applies that condition at 2. The creature card chooses one condition, not either at use. Burning is fire damage; Freezing is cold damage. Lightning attacks may explicitly leave Burning.

Before a physical attack against this creature is rolled, gain Physical resistance 3 against that attack only. Use the highest matching resistance. ID: monster-web-bridge

Choose up to 2 connected difficult-terrain squares within 3 squares on a surface it can see. They count as normal terrain until its next turn. Cannot bridge empty space, remove a wall or change occupied-square rules.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Frost races across the ground, raising brittle crusts of ice that catch at hurried feet.

Rules

ID: monster-lay-the-rime

Action: Maneuver

Make up to 3 connected empty ground squares within 3 squares difficult terrain for everyone until the start of this creature's next turn. Requires a supporting surface. No entry damage, automatic fall or bridge over empty space. Reusing this ability replaces its previous patch.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The victim pales as a stolen flush of warmth returns to the attacker’s face.

Rules

ID: monster-life-drink

Action: Main Action

Use the printed Life attack. If at least 1 HP is actually lost, the attacker recovers 1 HP on Standard or 2 HP on Strong, capped by the target’s actual HP loss and the attacker’s maximum. This explicitly grants undead-compatible restoration, not a healing spell. An uncommanded summon cannot trigger this attack. Defeat at 0 still happens immediately.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Stolen warmth returns color to the predator’s face.

Rules

ID: monster-life-taking-bite

Action: Main Action

At the printed outcomes, restore at most 1 or 2 HP to the attacker, never more than the HP actually lost by a living target to this attack after resistance. Life resistance on the recipient reduces this recovery, minimum 1 only if a positive amount is transferred. No recovery from a target that loses 0 HP or is not living. This transfer grants no wound treatment.

Actual damage, targeting and defense attribute are printed on the creature card.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Nothing breathes beneath the torn coat; nothing living looks through the visor.

Rules

ID: monster-lifeless-body

Action: Passive

The card must list its exact condition immunities; this trait grants no additional unlisted ones. It does not breathe or need food. Undead entries marked healing-harmed take a healing result as Life damage; constructs marked repair-only do not regain HP from ordinary healing. Neither rule prevents physical attacks from dealing their normal minimum damage.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Iron spurs lock against the threshold.

Rules

ID: monster-iron-gatekeeper-lock-the-feet

Action: Maneuver

Gain Stability 3 while on solid ground until its next turn; highest source only.

Limits: Costs its Maneuver; no extra action is granted.

The joints grind shut and the body becomes a single weight planted against the shove.

Rules

ID: monster-lock-the-frame

Action: Reaction

Before this creature is forcibly moved while on solid ground, gain Stability 3 for that forced movement only. Use the highest source. In a collision chain, declare before its Stability is deducted; prior collision damage still resolves. This does not resist Prone or grapples.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Its shoulders bunch behind the lowered tusks.

Rules

ID: monster-wild-boar-lower-the-tusks

Action: Maneuver

Gain Stability 1 until its next turn. Use the highest Stability; also gain 1 Boon on its next Tusks attack this turn (1 extra Bane on that target’s defense).

Limits: Costs its Maneuver; no extra action is granted.

A clipped order sends one companion into the opening before it closes.

Rules

ID: monster-commanding-step

Action: Maneuver

One willing active ally within 3 squares that can hear it may spend that ally’s Reaction to move up to 2 squares. Movement provokes normally and pays terrain costs. An uncommanded summon cannot act; summons have no Reaction to spend.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

A sharp line of light marks a boundary across the floor.

Rules

ID: monster-binding-circle

Action: Maneuver

Place up to 3 connected empty ground squares within 3 squares as difficult terrain until its next turn. No damage, wall or prohibition against crossing; all creatures pay the same terrain costs.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

It chooses its footing, shifting just far enough to clear the worst angle.

Rules

ID: monster-measured-step

Action: Maneuver

Move up to 2 squares without provoking from one visible enemy chosen before moving. Pay normal terrain costs and provoke normally from other enemies. Does not grant Hidden.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The hinges are teeth; the leather grain shivers like skin.

Rules

ID: monster-mimic-shell

Action: Passive

While still, this creature may resemble the ordinary object named in its entry. Reason search can expose the disguise using normal perception outcomes; touching or opening it reveals it before its next action, not a free attack. Once exposed, it needs concealment and a Hide action to become Hidden again.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

For a moment, the victim remembers a pain that has not happened yet.

Rules

ID: monster-mind-hammer

Action: Main Action; spell

Use the printed mental attack. Standard also applies Dazed 1; Strong applies Dazed 2. Ordinary turn-start action choices and end-turn decay apply. Damage and the condition use one outcome, not two rolls.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The struck limb goes rigid for one terrifying instant.

Rules

ID: monster-numbing-strike

Action: Main Action

The worst player defense outcome applies Paralyzed 1 as printed. This attack cannot be used on consecutive turns, regardless of outcome. This is not lasting petrification.

Actual damage, targeting and defense attribute are printed on the creature card.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The pack spreads without a sound; when you turn toward one set of teeth, another closes in.

Rules

ID: monster-pack-hunter

Action: Passive

When this creature attacks a target adjacent to another active ally, that attack has 1 additional Threat Bane (or 1 attack Boon when player-controlled). An unconscious, Paralyzed, or uncommanded summoned ally does not qualify. This does not grant an extra attack.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The shield’s rim bites into the earth beside the tomb.

Rules

ID: monster-barrow-guard-plant-the-shield

Action: Maneuver

Gain Stability 2 while on solid ground until its next turn; highest source only. This does not activate Shield Hunker.

Limits: Costs its Maneuver; no extra action is granted.

It spreads its stance and settles its weight into the ground.

Rules

ID: monster-brace-ground

Action: Maneuver

While standing on solid ground, gain Stability 3 until its next turn. Use the highest source only, never add sources.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

It gathers itself, then arrives in a rush of claws and weight.

Rules

ID: monster-pounce

Action: Main Action

Use the printed attack. If the creature moved at least 2 squares toward this target immediately before the attack this turn, Standard or Strong also makes the target Prone. Movement is paid normally, not supplied by Pounce.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

A barked order cuts through the noise, and a wavering fighter finds their footing.

Rules

ID: monster-rally

Action: Maneuver

Choose one ally within 3 squares that can hear this creature. Remove 1 Frightened from that ally. Alternatively, grant 1 Boon to the ally’s next attack before the start of this creature’s next turn (1 Threat Bane if an NPC attacks a player). Multiple copies of this named bonus do not stack. No free attack is granted.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

A sharp call catches the wounded companion's attention before pain can turn into panic.

Rules

ID: monster-rally-at-the-blow

Action: Reaction

After a visible willing ally within 3 squares takes HP damage from an attack, reduce that ally's Frightened by 1 if it can hear this creature. Then give it 1 Boon on its next defense before the start of this creature's next turn; for an NPC ally impose 1 Bane on the corresponding player attack. The defense benefit is consumed on that roll even if canceled and does not stack with itself. No healing or action is granted.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

A dry sound rises from the corpse, like someone knocking from inside a coffin.

Rules

ID: monster-rattle-bones

Action: Maneuver

One creature within 2 squares that can hear it gains Frightened 1 of this creature. Once per turn; no damage.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Loose objects jump and settle in all the wrong places.

Rules

ID: monster-rattle-room

Action: Maneuver

Move one unattended object of at most 1 Bulk within 3 squares into an empty square adjacent to its starting square. Cannot harm a creature, take a held item, trigger an attack or move anything fixed in place.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Its nose lifts, separating the sharp scent of fresh blood from the rest of the air.

Rules

ID: monster-blood-scent

Action: Maneuver

Learn the direction of the nearest Bleeding creature within 6 squares. This does not reveal Hidden, give an exact square or permit a sight-required attack against an unseen target.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Its wounded outline stretches into the nearest shadow and runs along the dark edge of the room.

Rules

ID: monster-recoil-into-shadow

Action: Reaction

After an attack resolves and deals HP damage to this creature, move up to 2 squares through connected dimly lit or dark squares without provoking. This creature must survive and remain capable. Pay normal terrain costs and obey occupancy; no passage through solid objects or automatic Hidden. No trigger from a free attack; no attack is granted.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The claws snag and drag; blood follows the withdrawing talons.

Rules

ID: monster-rending-blow

Action: Main Action

Use the printed attack. Standard also applies Bleeding 1; Strong applies Bleeding 2. Bleeding resolves and decays at the target’s turn end. This is not a wound roll unless the ordinary Dying rule calls for one.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

A whispered accusation rides the fading spell back toward the one who shaped it.

Rules

ID: monster-reproach-the-caster

Action: Reaction

After a spell attack resolves and deals HP damage to this creature, its visible caster within 6 squares gains Frightened 2 of this creature if the caster can hear it. This creature must survive and remain capable. No trigger from a free attack or another retaliatory effect. Frightened applies only while this creature is perceptible; the spell is not canceled.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

It catches a moving seam of water and lets the current carry its weight.

Rules

ID: monster-read-the-current

Action: Maneuver

While in water, move up to 3 squares using its printed swim speed without provoking from one visible enemy chosen before moving. Pay normal terrain costs and provoke normally from other enemies. On dry ground this Maneuver has no effect.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The goblin drops a shoulder, tumbles across the rubble and springs up beyond the answering blade.

Rules

ID: monster-roll-away

Action: Maneuver

Move up to 2 squares in a straight line without provoking opportunity attacks. Pay normal terrain costs from the 2-square allowance. Normal occupied-square restrictions apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Roots punch through the ground and lace together around the trespassers’ legs.

Rules

ID: monster-root-snare

Action: Main Action; spell

Choose the printed number of connected visible ground squares within range. They become difficult terrain until the start of this creature’s next turn. A creature in a chosen square when the ability resolves defends with Agility: Weak attack adds no condition, Standard applies Slowed 1, Strong Slowed 2. No damage; no repeated entry or turn-end attack. The creature’s card prints the controller’s attack attribute. Flying creatures above the ground are unaffected.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Thorns lace the knight’s boots to the soil.

Rules

ID: monster-briar-knight-root-the-stance

Action: Maneuver

Gain Stability 2 while on soil until its next turn; highest source only.

Limits: Costs its Maneuver; no extra action is granted.

The swarm opens around the incoming sweep, then folds back into a ragged cloud of wings or fur.

Rules

ID: monster-scatter-before-the-blast

Action: Reaction

Before an area attack that includes this creature is rolled, impose 1 Bane on that attack. Against an NPC area attack, grant 1 Boon to this creature's defense instead. This protection belongs to the swarm; a player area attack still uses one roll with the worst relevant target modifiers. No movement, new swarm or immunity is granted.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The shape bursts apart around the weapon and closes again as crawling fragments.

Rules

ID: monster-scatter-body

Action: Passive

The creature’s printed physical resistance represents its dispersed body. An area attack ignores that physical resistance, but not unrelated resistance. It still occupies its footprint and cannot overlap another creature at rest. No extra attacks from individual members; one HP pool and one turn.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

A spray of glowing cinders hangs between the creature and its pursuer.

Rules

ID: monster-scatter-embers

Action: Maneuver

One adjacent creature gains Burning 1. Once per turn; no immediate damage. The condition uses normal resistance and decay.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

A shove of its foot sends loose stones skittering into the approach.

Rules

ID: monster-scatter-stones

Action: Maneuver

Place difficult terrain in up to 2 connected empty ground squares within 2 squares until its next turn. Requires loose earth or stones. No entry damage or automatic falling.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Brittle hooks fall from its branches and catch across the path.

Rules

ID: monster-scatter-thorns

Action: Maneuver

Place difficult terrain in up to 3 connected empty ground squares within 2 squares until its next turn. No entry damage; ordinary clearing after the fight removes the thorns.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

While one head snaps forward, another turns toward the hand reaching for a spell or weapon.

Rules

ID: monster-second-head-watches

Action: Reaction

When a visible enemy within 2 squares starts an action that normally provokes an opportunity attack, make one free Basic Melee attack against it before the action resolves. Spend the Reaction. The 2-square reach applies only to this Reaction; the provoking action continues if its actor remains capable. No specialty attack or free-attack chain; cannot trigger from a free attack or its granted movement. This grants no extra Reaction and is an alternative to the normal adjacent opportunity attack.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

It starts moving a heartbeat before the strike, following a future the attacker has not yet reached.

Rules

ID: monster-seen-it-already

Action: Reaction

Before one attack from a visible attacker against this creature is rolled, impose 1 Bane on that attack. Against an NPC attack, grant 1 Boon to its single defense roll instead. This changes no target or outcome after dice have been rolled; it does not cancel the action.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

A coil or grasping limb closes around the target and braces against its struggling weight.

Rules

ID: monster-seizing-limbs

Action: Main Action

Use the printed attack. Standard also establishes Grappled 1; Strong establishes Grappled 2. A single holder’s contribution is replaced by its higher new result, not added to itself. Other holders stack normally. The holder suffers its own grapple contribution and cannot move while maintaining it. Release at any time without an action; death, unconsciousness or separation beyond the attack’s reach ends the hold. Force and external aid follow the core grapple rules.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Its many bones lock into one braced frame.

Rules

ID: monster-bone-colossus-set-the-frame

Action: Maneuver

Gain Stability 3 until its next turn; highest source only.

Limits: Costs its Maneuver; no extra action is granted.

The corpse lurches after the nearest warm body, dragging its ruined feet without ever looking away.

Rules

ID: monster-shambling-advance

Action: Maneuver

Move up to 2 squares toward a visible living creature within 6 squares; its next attack against that creature before turn end imposes 1 additional Bane on the player defense. For a player-controlled creature, gain 1 attack Boon instead. It must end closer to that creature than it began. For this movement only, treat difficult ground as normal; pay other costs and provoke normally. One attack only; repeated uses do not stack. This grants no attack and cannot be used while movement is prevented.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The surface peels away, leaving a useless handful while the body gathers again.

Rules

ID: monster-slough-skin

Action: Maneuver

Choose one holder and reduce that holder’s Grappled contribution by 1, also reducing this creature’s total Grappled rating by 1. End that hold if its contribution reaches 0. It must have a Maneuver available; cannot use this while Grappled 3. No damage or free movement.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

It turns at the cry beside it, bringing its whole body between the danger and the one it protects.

Rules

ID: monster-shelter-the-young

Action: Reaction

After a visible enemy ends voluntary movement adjacent to a willing ally within 3 squares, move up to 2 squares, ending adjacent to that ally. Pay normal terrain costs and provoke normally. This movement grants no attack or automatic protection; its body obstructs only the squares it actually occupies. Movement granted by a free attack cannot trigger it.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Light gathers over a companion like overlapping feathers, taking the harsh edge from the impact.

Rules

ID: monster-sheltering-light

Action: Reaction

Before one visible willing ally within 3 squares takes damage from an attack, grant that ally Physical resistance 2 for that attack only. Use the highest matching resistance, not an added reduction; minimum damage rules remain. This does not heal, transfer damage or grant resistance to other types.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The shield rises, scraping stone as its bearer crouches behind the rim.

Rules

ID: monster-shield-hunker

Action: Reaction

Before a shield-blockable attack resolves, spend Reaction to gain 1 defense Boon until the start of this creature’s next turn. For an NPC, apply 1 Bane to player attacks it can block instead. The DA decides whether the shield can block an attack. This stacks with Defend through ordinary Boon/Bane rules. No repeated activation adds another copy.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

It lowers its weight and makes the space in front of it suddenly too small.

Rules

ID: monster-barrel-through

Action: Maneuver

Push one adjacent creature 1 square. Apply Stability and normal collision rules. Once per turn; no separate damage.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Its feet drum across its own silk, drawing the whole web tight as it changes its hunting angle.

Rules

ID: monster-silken-scuttle

Action: Maneuver

Move up to 3 squares along existing web on a supporting surface, using its printed movement modes, without provoking from one visible enemy chosen before moving. Treat those web-covered squares as normal terrain for this movement only. Other opportunities apply. It cannot create a bridge, cross an occupied square or carry a grappled creature through this movement.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

As the pursuer lunges into reach, it ducks sideways through the space the rush left open.

Rules

ID: monster-slip-the-rush

Action: Reaction

After a visible enemy ends voluntary movement adjacent to this creature, move up to 1 square without provoking from that enemy. Other opportunity attacks and normal terrain costs apply. This movement grants no attack; it cannot trigger from forced movement or movement granted by a free attack.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Its outline folds into a seam of darkness and gathers again a few steps away.

Rules

ID: monster-shadow-slip

Action: Maneuver

Move up to 2 squares through connected dimly lit or dark squares without provoking. Normal terrain and occupancy rules apply. Does not grant Hidden or allow passage through solid objects.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

It slips beneath the surface with scarcely a ripple.

Rules

ID: monster-submerge

Action: Maneuver

Move up to 2 squares using its printed swim speed without provoking from one visible enemy chosen before moving. Pay normal terrain costs and provoke normally from other enemies. Water grants only the cover or concealment the scene actually provides; no automatic Hidden.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The outline goes thin as candle smoke and spills through a crack in the stone.

Rules

ID: monster-spectral-passage

Action: Maneuver

Move up to 2 squares, including through nonliving walls at movement cost 1, but finish in a visible legal unoccupied space. Cannot pass through living occupants or remain inside a wall. This voluntary movement can provoke when leaving reach. It does not grant invisibility, flight, damage immunity or passage through a ward expressly barring spirits.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

A sharp gesture splinters the incoming light into a cloud of harmless sparks.

Rules

ID: monster-spell-screen

Action: Reaction

Before one spell attack against this creature resolves, impose 1 Bane on that attack roll (or grant 1 defense Boon to its player controller). The protection belongs to this creature. For a player’s single AoE attack roll, include it when finding the worst target modifiers, as normal; do not make a separate roll or rescore outcomes for other targets. If players defend separately against an NPC area, it benefits only its own recipient. This is defensive interference, not cancellation; the resulting spell outcome still resolves.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Cracked ice bursts outward in a glittering spray that freezes across the attacker's skin.

Rules

ID: monster-splintering-rime

Action: Reaction

After an adjacent attacker's attack resolves and deals HP damage to this creature, apply Freezing 1 to that attacker. This creature must survive and remain capable. No trigger from a free attack or another retaliatory effect. This is a condition, not another attack.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

A slow shake of its crown releases a drifting veil of pale spores that hangs between the trunks.

Rules

ID: monster-spore-curtain

Action: Maneuver

Fill up to 3 connected empty squares within 3 squares with spores that give partial obstruction until the start of this creature's next turn. Apply 1 Bane when that obstruction lies in an attack's path, following the normal targeting rules. The spores do not grant Hidden or cause a condition or damage. Reusing this ability replaces its previous cloud.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

It folds into the broken light, leaving only a leaf moving where it stood.

Rules

ID: monster-stalking-step

Action: Maneuver

Move up to 2 squares without provoking from one visible enemy chosen before moving, ending in a square with cover or concealment from that enemy. Pay normal terrain costs and provoke normally from other enemies. Does not grant Hidden; a separate Hide action still needs concealment and a roll when uncertain.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Coals brighten inside its body and a hot breath spills between teeth or iron seams.

Rules

ID: monster-stoke-the-core

Action: Maneuver

Add 1 Fire damage to its next damaging Main Action attack before the end of this turn. Apply it once per target damaged by that attack, using the normal mixed-damage resistance and minimum rules. This grants no extra attack or Burning. Repeated uses do not add more Fire damage.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Gray veins climb from the victim’s feet while the creature holds an unblinking stare.

Rules

ID: monster-stone-stare

Action: Main Action; spell

One target within the printed range that can see the creature: Weak Slowed 1; Standard Slowed 2; Strong Paralyzed 1. No HP damage. A target may avert their eyes until their next turn: the gaze cannot select them, but they have 1 Bane on attacks against this creature and defenses against its attacks during that time. Declare before the gaze resolves. There is no permanent petrification or instant death in this card.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

It waits for a tell in the stance, then turns its attention to the exposed line.

Rules

ID: monster-watch-the-opening

Action: Maneuver

Its next attack before the end of this turn imposes 1 additional Bane on player defense, or gains 1 Boon when player-controlled. One attack only; no stacking with itself.

Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed limits apply.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The blow leaves thought and motion briefly out of step.

Rules

ID: monster-stunning-strike

Action: Main Action

The printed attack applies Dazed. Retained action categories are selected at turn start; do not retroactively remove spent actions.

Actual damage, targeting and defense attribute are printed on the creature card.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

Use the printed attack against up to two different creatures within its printed reach, including allies if deliberately selected. Each player target defends separately. A player-controlled sweep rolls once at the worst target modifiers. This replaces, rather than accompanies, a single-target attack.

Limits: Only creatures whose entries list this ability possess it. Printed entry values and restrictions apply; no ability grants unlisted actions.

Apply Stability, terrain costs and normal collision damage; no separate attack damage. Cannot trigger from a free attack or another retaliatory effect.

Creature procedure · @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.da-rules.JournalEntry.fcfeb03f877503a3.JournalEntryPage.743fa3bd946d24fb]{Monster ability index}

The hound lifts its nose and finds the freshest thread of scent.

Rules

Gain 1 Boon on its next Reason scent-tracking roll before turn end; needs a scent trail. No automatic discovery.

Limits: Costs its Maneuver; no extra action is granted.

Rules

ID: monster-hill-ogre-threatening-roar

Action: Maneuver

One hearing creature within 3 squares gains Frightened 1 of the ogre; once per turn.

Limits: Costs its Maneuver; no extra action is granted.
